# Tool DSL reference

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen_dsl_doc.py from src/maris3d/dsl/tools.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

The model answers with ONE JSON object: `{"calls":[ {...}, {...} ]}`. Each call has a `"tool"` name and that tool's arguments.
At most 40 calls per answer (`maxItems` of the schema). `maris3d.dsl.tools.compile_calls(doc)` turns the document into a Blender Python script
(Blender 5.2 API). Unknown or odd arguments are ignored, not fatal. Vectors are `[x, y, z]` in metres (Blender units); rotations are in degrees
(`rotation_deg`). Objects are referred to by the `name` they were given.

Example:

```json
{"calls":[
  {"tool":"add_primitive","shape":"cube","name":"Box","location":[0,0,1]},
  {"tool":"set_material","object":"Box","name":"Red","color":[0.8,0.1,0.1]},
  {"tool":"add_light","kind":"SUN","location":[4,-4,6],"energy":3},
  {"tool":"add_camera","location":[6,-6,4],"rotation_deg":[63,0,45]}
]}
```

There are 28 tools in the executor. The model is offered the 26 it was trained on (`TOOLS.json`); `clone_object` and `snow` are run only from code (the scene harness), never from a model answer. Types: `number`, `integer`, `string`, `boolean`, `vec3` = array of 3 numbers, `[...]` = array.

|---|---|---|

| `depth` | number |  |
